description.short: Darker and fuller in body than spring harvests, featuring a nutty profile and mellow aromatic character
description.overview: Harvested after the summer monsoons subside when leaves reach maturity — producing a less airy and floral, but richer, amber-tinted cup with nutty depth.
description.leaf: Dark brown, denser leaf than spring flushes
description.aroma: Nutty, more subdued than the first or second flush
description.taste: Full-bodied, nutty, softer and less astringent than spring harvests; accommodates milk well
description.processing: Harvesting mature autumn leaves → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: The autumnal harvest gained recognition as a distinct category later than the first and second flushes, as buyers began appreciating the seasonal variance of the terroir throughout the year.
history.development: Due to softer aroma profiles, autumnal teas were historically viewed as secondary, but over time found loyal followers who favor comforting, rounded black teas.
history.modern: Today, Darjeeling Autumnal is an affordable alternative to prized spring lots, and its fuller body makes it amenable to pairing with milk.
interestingFacts: Unlike the first and second flushes, which are almost universally drunk pure, autumnal flush has enough depth to take a dash of milk or be used in spiced chai.
